doc.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: High school rock bands and amplification problems
summary: Playing trumpet in rock bands in high school, awkward keys and being overpowered by amplified instruments.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And what was your first actual ensemble experience where you started to make a few dollars?

Well I was working in high school with some bands, mostly rock bands. There was one band that I played in which was just two electric guitars and bass guitar and drums and trumpet. And I remember because they used to play everything in the key of E and A. So I used to, I actually borrowed this cornet that I could like play, I think if I pushed the slides all the way in I could kind of play in — rather than have to play in F sharp and B, I could play in F and B flat or something like that. I don’t know. But it worked out some crazy way. And I had to play, you know it was good experience just to play. I was always playing all kind of different music from the start. The downside of it was that I started developing this problem which really caught up with me later which was that playing with these amplified instruments — I mean back then the amplification thing was pretty new. And people didn’t do the sound systems people used, and the micing wasn’t that sophisticated. And usually if you were a horn playing with amplified instruments you were kind of at a disadvantage.
